subject: EU-W3: Staged microcode + driver harmonization — customer impact and ops checklist
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme.com, support@acme.com
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-15T08:00:00Z
Subject: EU-W3: Staged microcode + driver harmonization — customer impact and ops checklist

Hi Sam and Acme ops team,

We wanted to give you an early heads-up about a planned maintenance window in EU-W3 next week. Objective: harmonize GPU microcode and driver versions across the host pool to address a corner-case model memory growth observed under sustained KV-cache-heavy workloads. The work is staged to minimize disruption and preserve KV cache where possible.

Planned window (staged):
- Start: 2028-11-20 01:00 UTC
- End: 2028-11-21 08:00 UTC
- Scope: subset of hosts serving EU-W3 general-purpose and inference-optimized pools

What to expect:
- Brief token-level latency blips during per-host restarts (typical < 2s for streaming connections; short interruptions possible).
- We will perform rolling restarts with sticky routing; most requests will be routed to warm hosts.
- We will preserve KV cache where supported; in a small number of cases, KV cache will be rebuilt (clients may see slightly higher latency for first requests after failover).

Attached: release notes and ops checklist (includes exact host ranges and mitigation steps).

Action items for Acme:
1) Confirm whether you want a preemptive drain for long-lived sessions (we can coordinate a soft drain for the 20% of capacity you flagged).
2) Provide any blackout windows we should avoid.

I'll be the point of contact during the window; Grace will run the orchestration and Marcus will own rollbacks. Soojin will monitor quality/regression signals. If you'd like us to schedule a short pre-window call, let me know times that work.

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: euw3-microcode-release-notes-v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: euw3-ops-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme.com
Date: 2028-11-15T12:34:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-W3: Staged microcode + driver harmonization — customer impact and ops checklist

Rafael,

Thanks for the heads up. A couple quick Qs from our side:
- We run a set of long-lived streaming sessions for user inference between 06:00-14:00 UTC. Can you guarantee maintenance will avoid that window for hosts primarily handling our traffic?
- If KV cache is rebuilt for some requests, will there be any increased cost implications (e.g., additional token generation or retries)?

We'd appreciate a 30-minute pre-window sync to confirm the runbook. Tuesday 2028-11-20 at 00:00 UTC is tight for us; can we do Monday 2028-11-19 17:00 UTC instead?

—Sam
Lead SRE, Acme Corp

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-15T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-W3: Staged microcode + driver harmonization — customer impact and ops checklist

Sam — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and updated plan below.

On 2028-11-15 at 12:34, Sam Patel wrote:
> Rafael,
>
> Thanks for the heads up. A couple quick Qs from our side:
> - We run a set of long-lived streaming sessions for user inference between 06:00-14:00 UTC. Can you guarantee maintenance will avoid that window for hosts primarily handling our traffic?
> - If KV cache is rebuilt for some requests, will there be any increased cost implications (e.g., additional token generation or retries)?

We can do the following to minimize impact to your 06:00-14:00 UTC window:
- We will not schedule restarts for any host where your tenancy currently has 50%+ of the active sessions during your blackout. Those hosts will be deferred to the final tail-stage (outside your window).
- For long-lived sessions we can enable soft-drain which will allow new connections to land on other hosts while letting existing streams finish. That reduces forced disconnects.

KV cache and cost:
- Rebuilding KV cache will only affect the initial requests that re-populate the cache. The increase in token usage should be negligible for most workloads; we do not expect a material billing delta. If you run high-volume batched replay jobs immediately after restarts, that pattern could cause measurable extra tokens — we suggest scheduling batch-heavy jobs outside the restart of hosts serving your tenancy.

Pre-window sync: Monday 2028-11-19 17:00 UTC works for our team; we'll send a calendar invite.

Ops runbook highlights (excerpt):
- Stage A (low-risk): apply microcode to 10% of pool, validate health & KV persistence, 30m soak.
- Stage B (broad rollout): 50% of pool in parallel groups with sticky routing safeguards.
- Stage C (tail): deferred hosts serving long-lived sessions.
- Rollback criteria: >3% request error rate increase sustained for 10 minutes, or persistent KV cache rebuilding across >20% of hosts in a group.

If you want, Grace can attach a mapping of your tenancy to host groups prior to the call.

Regards,
Rafael

[Quoted attachment: euw3-ops-checklist.xlsx]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-22T16:18:00Z
Subject: RE: EU-W3: Staged microcode + driver harmonization — customer impact and ops checklist

Hi Sam — follow-up after the window.

Summary: the staged microcode + driver harmonization completed on 2028-11-21 06:42 UTC. We executed the plan in three stages (A/B/C) as discussed. For your tenancy:
- No forced disconnects detected for long-lived streams in your primary host group (soft-drain honored).
- KV cache rebuilds observed on ~3 hosts serving Acme; these caused transient latency increases for 1–3 requests while caches warmed.
- No rollback criteria were met; overall error rates were within expected bounds.

Attachments & postmortem: please find the execution log and a short post-maintenance note in the drive link below. If you'd like an internal postmortem with your SREs, we can schedule a 45-minute review next week.

Execution artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/euw3/microcode-harmonization/execution-log
Status: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/EUW3-2028-11

Thanks for aligning on the schedule and the blackout. Let us know if you saw anything on your side we should investigate further.

Best,
Grace
Senior Manager, Operations
Redwood Inference
